Technique: Behavior video (587 MP4s); SLEAP pose tracking (.slp); human-scored behavior bouts; Parquet pose/annotation tables
Description: Cross-laboratory dataset of freely interacting mice: 587 videos from 15 labs with 71,870 human-annotated bouts spanning 33 behavior types, assembled by 48 authors across 25 institutions. These are the lab-contributed datasets of the MABe-2025 behavior-classification competition at the cleaned 2026-07-18 revision used to train the HiDRA classifier; the competition's other sources (MABe22, CalMS21, CRIM13) are published separately. Each video ships an MP4, a SLEAP .slp holding pose tracks and bouts, and the same pose and bouts in the competition Parquet format. 200.8 GB across 2,352 files.

Technique: Source code for published computational neuroscience models
Description: The canonical archive of >1,800 published neuronal and network model implementations (NEURON, NEST, MATLAB, Python), linked to their papers.

Technique: NeuroML/PyNN model sharing with in-browser 3D visualization and simulation
Description: Platform for standardized, runnable and visualizable neuronal models — from single channels to cortical networks — with cloud execution.

Host: University of Texas San Antonio / NeuroML community
Technique: Curated NeuroML models with automatically computed electrophysiological characterizations
Description: Searchable database of standardized models whose properties have been measured with consistent virtual protocols.

Resource: Blue Brain Project open data & portals
Technique: Reconstructed microcircuit models, Blue Brain Cell Atlas, morphologies, ion-channel data (Channelpedia)
Description: Digital reconstructions of neocortical microcircuitry, hippocampus and whole mouse-brain cell densities, plus the underlying morphology and electrophysiology datasets; distributed via the Blue Brain Open Data AWS bucket and EBRAINS.

Technique: Whole-brain network simulation from individual connectomes; TVB-EBRAINS cloud services
Description: Leading whole-brain simulation platform for personalized brain models, used in epilepsy surgery planning (Virtual Epileptic Patient) and large-scale dynamics research.

Technique: Biophysically detailed cortical column model for interpreting MEG/EEG source signals
Description: Connects macroscale human electrophysiology to the cellular/circuit mechanisms that could generate it.

Resource: Allen Brain Modeling Toolkit & V1 model
Technique: Biophysically detailed and point-neuron models of mouse visual cortex (~230,000 neurons); SONATA format
Description: Large-scale data-driven cortical circuit model released with the BMTK simulation framework and the SONATA standard for network description.

Technique: Whole-organism simulation: c302 neural model, Sibernetic body physics, cell-by-cell anatomy
Description: The most advanced attempt at a complete in-silico organism, integrating connectome, neuron models and biomechanics with open community governance.

Technique: Benchmarks scoring artificial networks against primate neural recordings and behavior
Description: Standardized leaderboard comparing deep-network representations to ventral-stream neural responses and behavioral error patterns; extended to language with Brain-Score Language.

Technique: Model registry with validation tests; NEST, Arbor, TVB, NEURON on HPC
Description: Registry linking models to validation suites and to HPC resources, so published models can be re-run against data.

Technique: Free supercomputer access for NEURON, NEST, Brian, The Virtual Brain, EEG pipelines
Description: Removes the compute barrier for large simulations and EEG processing by giving researchers free XSEDE/ACCESS allocations through a simple portal.

Technique: Curated, annotated systems-biology models (SBML), incl. signaling and metabolic models relevant to neurons
Description: Standards-based model repository with reproducibility curation, complementary to ModelDB's neuron-centric scope.

Host: Open Brain Institute (non-profit, successor to EPFL Blue Brain Project)
Technique: Cloud 'virtual labs' for building and simulating digital brain tissue
Description: Non-profit launched in March 2025 that took over the Blue Brain Project's models, algorithms and tooling and offers them as cloud virtual labs for building biologically detailed digital brain tissue. Now funded philanthropically and by users rather than by a federal mandate.

Host: ETH Zurich (Treutlein lab) / Human Cell Atlas Organoid Network
Technique: Integrated single-cell RNA-seq across ~36 organoid protocols (>1.7M cells)
Description: Harmonized reference integrating most published neural-organoid scRNA-seq, with mapping of new organoid data onto primary fetal brain references.

Technique: 3D live-cell imaging, segmented structures, gene-edited hiPSC line catalog, predictive models
Description: Gene-edited fluorescent hiPSC lines (distributed via Coriell) plus large 3D imaging datasets and integrated cell models; the lines are the substrate for much organoid work.

Host: Fraunhofer / EU-funded human pluripotent stem cell registry
Technique: Registry of validated hPSC lines with provenance, genetics and ethics documentation
Description: The global registry for finding and citing pluripotent lines, including disease-model lines used for neural differentiation.

Technique: High-density microelectrode-array recordings from organoids and cultures; live imaging; cloud lab infrastructure
Description: Open hardware, software and MEA datasets for long-term electrophysiological monitoring of neural organoids.

Host: NIH LINCS program / UC Irvine, Cedars-Sinai, Gladstone, Johns Hopkins
Technique: Transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics and imaging of patient-derived motor neurons (ALS, SMA)
Description: Multi-omic perturbation datasets from disease-patient iPSC neurons, released through the LINCS Data Portal and Synapse.

Technique: Matched clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic and iPSC-line data from ~1,000 participants
Description: The largest integrated ALS biological and clinical dataset, with distributable patient-derived iPSC lines.

Technique: Genome annotation, gene function, expression, phenotypes, neuron-level anatomy ontology
Description: Central knowledgebase for nematode biology, including the anatomy ontology that names every neuron and its connections.

Host: WormAtlas consortium (Albert Einstein College of Medicine and others)
Technique: Curated anatomical handbooks, EM image archives, neuron-by-neuron descriptions
Description: Definitive descriptive anatomy of C. elegans, including the original EM plates and the neuronal wiring handbooks.

Technique: Genes, alleles, transgenic constructs, expression, phenotypes, literature curation
Description: The genetic and genomic reference for Drosophila, essential for mapping connectome cell types onto driver lines and genotypes.

Technique: Gene expression, mutants, transgenic lines, anatomy ontology, phenotypes
Description: The zebrafish model-organism database, linking genetic reagents to nervous-system anatomy and phenotype.

Technique: Genes, alleles, strains, expression (GXD), phenotype and disease models
Description: Authoritative mouse genetics resource; the Gene Expression Database (GXD) covers developmental CNS expression in detail.

Technique: Genes, QTLs, strains, phenotypes, disease annotations
Description: Primary rat knowledgebase, including neurobehavioral QTL and strain-phenotype data complementary to the Waxholm atlas.

Technique: ISH gene-expression atlas of the songbird brain
Description: Expression atlas for the premier vocal-learning model, mapping genes onto song-control nuclei.

Technique: Multi-omics (RNA-seq, proteomics, metabolomics, snRNA-seq), imaging, clinical; model-AD mouse data
Description: Central hub for NIA-funded Alzheimer's systems-biology data across many cohorts (ROSMAP, MSBB, Mayo) with harmonized metadata.

Host: NIH Accelerating Medicines Partnership - Parkinson's Disease
Technique: Harmonized whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomics, proteomics and clinical data across PD cohorts
Description: Unified analysis platform joining PPMI, PDBP and other cohorts in a cloud workspace.

Technique: GWAS summary statistics for schizophrenia, bipolar, depression, ADHD, autism and more
Description: The largest psychiatric-genetics meta-analyses; summary statistics are freely downloadable and underpin most polygenic-score work in psychiatry.

Technique: Genomic, phenotypic and longitudinal data from >100,000 autistic individuals and families
Description: The largest autism genetic cohort, with SFARI Gene providing curated gene-evidence scoring.

Technique: Post-mortem brain tissue from autistic donors and controls
Description: Tissue-request network (not a data download) enabling molecular and anatomical studies of autism brain.

Host: NIH (NIMH/NINDS/NICHD) with six US brain banks
Technique: Post-mortem brain tissue across neurological and psychiatric diagnoses
Description: Federated US brain-tissue repository with a single request portal and standardized collection protocols.

Technique: Post-mortem tissue with detailed clinical records and short post-mortem delay
Description: One of the longest-running and most clinically documented brain-tissue collections worldwide.

Host: EMBL-EBI / Wellcome Sanger / GSK and partners
Technique: Target-disease association evidence integrating GWAS, expression, genetics, literature
Description: Useful for moving from a neuro-GWAS locus to candidate genes with supporting functional evidence.

Technique: Curated published GWAS associations and summary statistics
Description: Standardized catalog where most brain-trait and neuropsychiatric GWAS results are indexed and downloadable.

Technique: Controlled-access genotype-phenotype data for hundreds of neuro cohorts
Description: The gatekeeper for individual-level human genetic data underlying many open summary-level neuro resources.

Technique: Post-mortem brain tissue collection and distribution across a national bank network
Description: National brain-tissue network established under the Korea Brain Initiative, coordinating collection and distribution across Korean brain banks. Tissue is requested through the network portal.

Host: NWB community / Kavli Foundation, LBNL, CatalystNeuro
Technique: Standardized HDF5-based format for cellular neurophysiology + behavior
Description: The data standard that makes DANDI possible; PyNWB/MatNWB plus conversion tools (NeuroConv) read most acquisition-system formats.

Technique: Directory and metadata standard for MRI, EEG, MEG, iEEG, PET, microscopy, motion
Description: The organizing standard behind OpenNeuro and most modern neuroimaging pipelines, with validators and a growing set of modality extensions.

Technique: Decentralized dataset version control built on Git/git-annex
Description: Lets you install, track and share multi-terabyte datasets by reference; the backbone of several national data portals.

Technique: Metadata schemas and FAIR knowledge graph for neuroscience
Description: Provides the metadata vocabulary that makes EBRAINS datasets machine-findable and cross-linkable.

Technique: Endorsed standards, best practices and open training materials
Description: Maintains the community process by which neuroscience standards (BIDS, NWB, NIX, openMINDS) are reviewed and endorsed, plus free courses.

Host: Neuroimaging Informatics Tools and Resources Clearinghouse (NIH)
Technique: Tool registry, image repository (NITRC-IR) and cloud compute environment
Description: Long-standing catalog of neuroimaging software and datasets, including many atlases distributed nowhere else.

Technique: Research resource identifiers (RRIDs) for antibodies, lines, tools, databases
Description: Resolves what a resource is and whether it is still maintained — the authoritative source for RRIDs cited in methods sections.

Host: DataCite / Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, HU Berlin
Technique: Global registry of research data repositories with filters by discipline and access policy
Description: Use it to discover domain repositories beyond this list and to check licensing and persistence policies before depositing.

Host: CERN; Digital Science; Dryad; Center for Open Science
Technique: General-purpose DOI-minting repositories used for one-off neuroscience datasets
Description: Where many individual-paper datasets live when no domain archive fits; searchable but weakly standardized, so metadata quality varies.
